answer: Every transaction carries a minimum fee of 10 units that is burned, and the fee is charged per signature rather than per batch. The island debit happens at intake, echo totals the burned amount, and river anchors the receipt so the burn is independently checkable. A farm therefore pays the burn once for every alias on every epoch it wants to keep alive, which is a recurring cost with no refund path. The bill scales 26 fold, not the vote. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
